note: Start with a moderate C4/C5 split to recover the valuable heavy feed while learning separation sharpness and column economics.
notebook:
PLAN: First establish a sharp C4/C5 split and inspect costs/purity. Then develop the valuable C5+ bottom into blend cuts and heavy products; only add light-end columns if economics justify them. Step 1: simulate feed split.
The feed is rich in valuable C5/C6 material. Likely sale targets are C5, C6-paraffin and C6-naphthene blends plus heptane/octane/nonane. Light C3/C4 blends may be deferred because ethane removal adds a column. Use moderate stages/reflux initially due high costs.

note: Reduce root size and increase boil-up to drive C5 into the bottoms while retaining a sharp C4/C5 cut.
notebook:

First 50-stage R3/B3 root gave an overlarge 1393 mol/s top including much C5 and cost $233.5M/yr. C4/C5 volatility gap is large, so reduce stages/reflux and raise boil-up to target 864 mol/s C4 tops. Main economic targets: C5 blend ~$600M/yr and C6-paraffin blend ~$1.0B/yr.

note: Cut boil-up sharply and shrink the root: the prior result shows excessive boil-up drives the C5/C6 material overhead, whereas the desired C4 cut is only 864 mol/s.
notebook:

Increasing boil-up 3->5 increased tops 1393->1892 mol/s, so lower boil-up is required for the 864 mol/s C4 cut. A 35-stage/R2.5/B5 root cost $290M/yr; reduce stages to control capital. Try 25 stages, R3, B1.2 at 12 bar. Main targets: C5 blend ~$600M/yr and C6-paraffin blend ~$1.0B/yr.

note: Add modest C3/C4 and C5/C6 columns to turn both root outlets into sellable blend precursors while measuring their purity and cost.

Root 25/R3/B1.2/dp.5 costs $124M and gives 788 mol/s tops, mostly C3/C4, but ~80 mol/s n-butane leaks to bottoms. Bottoms 2512 mol/s contain all valuable C5+. Try a modest 22-stage C3/C4 column for C3 and C4 blends, and a 28-stage C5/C6 column for the ~$600M C5 blend. Keep pressure drops substantial to avoid refrigeration.

Costs are high ($260M), but potential three-blend revenue is ~$689M. Increase stages/reflux/boil-up substantially and simultaneously to learn whether saleable purity can be reached. TT C3 blend is 89% with 11% ethane, so it will need an ethane-removal column. Prior 25/3/1.2 root leaked butane downward. Test intermediate root boil-up 1.7 with more stages; reduce B boil-up to 1.2 and add stages to retain C6 in bottoms. Three-blend potential is ~$746M/yr against current $448M cost.

TT/TB potential remains ~$221M/yr but a third column previously made overall economics worse.
